title: Knower of the unseen
cue: What the Prophet ﷺ taught Abu Bakr for morning, evening and bedtime
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ فَاطِرَ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ، عَالِمَ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ، رَبَّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَمَلِيكَهُ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ نَفْسِي، وَشَرِّ الشَّيْطَانِ وَشِرْكِهِ
transliteration: Allaahumma faatiras-samawaati wal-ard, 'aalimal-ghaybi wash-shahaadah, rabba kulli shay'in wamaleekah, ashhadu an laa ilaha illaa ant, a'oodhu bika min sharri nafsee, washarrish-shaytaani washirkih
translation: O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Lord and Sovereign of everything: I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek refuge with You from the evil of my own self, and from the evil of Satan and his call to associate others with You.

witnesses.name: shamela
witnesses.ref: Sunan Abi Dawud, ed. Muhyi al-Din Abd al-Hamid, hadith 5067: https://shamela.ws/book/1726/6927

usage.evidence: Abu Bakr asked for words to say morning and evening; the Prophet ﷺ taught him these and said: say it in the morning, in the evening and when you lie down (Abu Dawud 5067). Al-Tirmidhi relates it with the first two phrases in the other order (3392) and calls it hasan sahih.
